rule: Antyodaya Anna Yojana households are entitled to 35 kg of food grains per household per month under the National Food Security Act.
Priority Household beneficiaries are entitled to 5 kg of food grains per person per month under the National Food Security Act.
Under the Maharashtra Government Resolution dated 17 December 2013, an annual family income limit of Rs. 44,000 was specified for PHH beneficiary selection in rural areas.
Under the Maharashtra Government Resolution dated 17 December 2013, an annual family income limit of Rs. 59,000 was specified for PHH beneficiary selection in urban areas.
The Central Government provides NFSA food grain entitlements free of cost to AAY households and PHH beneficiaries for five years beginning 1 January 2024.

The original NFSA central issue prices were Rs. 3 per kg for rice, Rs. 2 per kg for wheat and Rs. 1 per kg for coarse grains. These are historical prices and should not be treated as current prices under the free-grain notification.
quantity_or_limit: Historical: Rice Rs. 3, Wheat Rs. 2, Coarse grains Rs. 1 per kg

rule: Under One Nation One Ration Card, NFSA beneficiaries can collect their entitled food grains from any participating ePoS-enabled Fair Price Shop across States and Union Territories.
Beneficiaries can use their existing NFSA AAY or PHH ration cards when migrating to another State. They do not need to surrender their existing ration card or obtain a new card for portability.
quantity_or_limit: Existing ration card; no new card required for portability

rule: Authentication methods include fingerprint-based biometric authentication, IRIS, Aadhaar OTP and PDS OTP. States and Union Territories have been advised not to deny food grains to genuine beneficiaries when biometric authentication, Aadhaar seeding, ePoS devices or network connectivity fail.
quantity_or_limit: Fingerprint, IRIS, Aadhaar OTP and PDS OTP

rule: The One Nation One Ration Card helpline provides information and assistance regarding ration portability.
The eldest woman in an eligible household who is at least 18 years old is considered the head of the household for issuing a ration card.
quantity_or_limit: Eldest woman aged 18 years or above

rule: If a household has no woman aged 18 years or above, the eldest male member may be treated as the head of the household until a female member attains 18 years of age.
quantity_or_limit: Female member becomes eligible as head at 18 years

rule: Pregnant women and lactating mothers are entitled to free nutritious meals through prescribed government programmes and maternity benefits of not less than Rs. 6,000, subject to applicable scheme provisions.
quantity_or_limit: Nutritious meals and maternity benefit of at least Rs. 6,000

rule: Children aged 6 months to 6 years are entitled to free nutritious meals through the Integrated Child Development Services programme.
quantity_or_limit: Free nutritious meals through Anganwadi centres

rule: Children aged 6 to 14 years are entitled to nutritious meals through the prescribed school meal programme.
Higher nutritional norms are prescribed for malnourished children up to 6 years of age under the NFSA nutrition provisions.
An aggrieved NFSA beneficiary can approach the District Grievance Redressal Officer for complaints concerning non-delivery of entitled food grains or meals.
A complainant dissatisfied with a DGRO order can appeal to the State Food Commission under the grievance redressal mechanism of the NFSA.

Maharashtra ration card holders can contact the Food and Civil Supplies Department for Public Distribution System complaints through its toll-free helplines. The ONORC helpline is separately available for portability assistance.
authority: Maharashtra Food and Civil Supplies Department
